sources.inspection: Owner record read: nominal front width 108m, quadrangle-inclusive depth 120m, building height 24m. Bath-stone garden elevations differ from Portland-stone east refacing. Balcony appearances date from 1851; the east refacing occurred in 1913. These are nominal controls, not a survey of each projection or flagstaff.
sources.visualInspection: Linked aerial opened successfully as an image in the browser, but screenshot capture timed out; no aerial pixel review claimed.

sources.inspection: Owner history read: Blore’s 1847–1849 east wing closed the open courtyard and introduced the balcony at Prince Albert’s suggestion. This contradicts the Qualla story claim that the balcony was first added during the 1913 refacing. Preserve the story unchanged; record the discrepancy as research evidence.

Owner architectural history read: Nash extended the central block and rebuilt the two eastern wings; Blore enclosed the courtyard. East frontage was later refaced in Portland stone; this page describes completion in 1914, while other owner/heritage records cite 1913. No false precision about construction completion dates.

Primary architectural listing read in full. Supports quadrangle form; east facade bay rhythm 3:7:3:7:3, mezzanines, rusticated archways, giant Corinthian orders, pediments and parapets. Distinguishes courtyard elevations/porticoes, garden bow and temple conservatories, Ambassadors’ Court and attached ballroom. Slate/lead roofs; warm Bath-stone west and Caen-stone courtyard contrast with east frontage. Fine sculpture and unseen engineering remain estimates.

ambassadorsPortico.interpretation: The native6m projection at X−66..−61.45/Z2.35..11.27 represents an open columned porch. Authored main low wall is recessed to the rear line; original native outline remains unchanged as evidence. A buried own platform, real free columns, entablature and pitched pedimented roof occupy the projection.

geographicReview.notes: Own connected palace outline 52776563341652 and 19 native component parts retain three courtyard voids; separate Royal Mews/Riding School, memorial, gates and detached neighbors are excluded. +X runs north-west along the east frontage and +Z north-east toward the Mall. Own native east range is about 107.9 m wide; owner nominal controls are 108 m frontage,120 m quadrangle-inclusive depth and 24 m main height. Projections and attached wings are retained beyond the nominal rectangle. Four full local originals plus primary owner/heritage descriptions establish the two principal fronts and southern court; aerial pixel capture was unavailable and is not claimed. Original 6 m native porch projection is interpreted as an open colonnade: its low body wall is recessed, with a separate buried platform/free columns/pitched temple roof and steps occupying the projection. Native evidence is preserved unchanged. Four original Terrarium tiles precede geometry; all 37249 samples, source hashes, datum and PNG 16 round trip verify. Native outlines span about−1.174..+0.470 m relative to the 6.4092 m dry eastern datum. Buried−4 m foundations and own terraces close sampled authored perimeters; host ground is unchanged. Source curvature simplification is bounded and measured above, with the open-porch interpretation separate. All actual visible garden/porch tread checks pass. Thin 3 m courtyard paving covers the exact three native courtyard areas and clears independent ground at all 1316 runtime triangle centroids. Terrain/contact engineering is approximate. Bounded preview; footprint replacement disabled.
